TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Governance & risk management
controls: There is a role with information-security oversight that sets direction for the organization's security program.
There is a formal, documented and implemented information-risk management program.
The risk management program has a dedicated owner responsible for maintaining and reviewing it.
There is an information security policy, approved by management and reviewed periodically.
Information security roles and responsibilities are defined and documented.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: People & personnel security
controls: Job applicants are screened, including prior-employment and reference checks.
Staff are required to sign a non-disclosure agreement and an acceptable-use policy.
Access rights are automatically removed, or promptly adjusted, when someone's employment or role changes.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Information asset management
controls: There is a formal asset-management program with an inventory of critical assets, including any assets accessible to third parties.
Ownership of information assets is formally assigned.
There is a formal information-classification policy.
The asset-management program covers the handling, disposal, destruction and reuse of media.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Devices, mobile & remote access
controls: Sensitive data is encrypted when copied to removable media.
Remote access to systems, applications or network devices requires multi-factor authentication and encryption.
Physical devices and systems are inventoried.
There are processes to ensure the secure physical transport of removable media.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Secure development lifecycle
controls: There is a maintained, up-to-date development methodology covering techniques, delivery methods, architectures and security standards.

Quality assurance in the development lifecycle covers: assessing development risks; confirming security requirements are defined; confirming the agreed security controls were built; and verifying they are effectively met.
There is a clearly defined process for version control over development software.

There is a secure development environment that accounts for data sensitivity, applicable requirements, existing controls, environment segregation, access control, change monitoring, offsite backups and data movement in and out.
Software developers receive periodic secure-coding training.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Release, testing & code security
controls: Post-implementation reviews, including information security, are conducted for all new systems.
There is a final security assessment on applications before they go live.
Customers are provided with the results of that final security assessment on request.
There are periodic reviews for outdated protocols and libraries.
Controls are in place to ensure confidential or live data is never used in testing.
Source code and data in development environments have unnecessary sensitive information removed (credentials, developer comments, organizational detail).

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Application & environment segregation
controls: Developers do not have access to production systems and data.
Test, development and production systems are hosted in separate environments.
Systems used to store or process your data are separated from systems processing other customers' data.
Web-server communications are encrypted, with non-repudiation ensured via digital certificates.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Identity & access management
controls: There is a formal access-control policy: role-based access, a unique ID per individual, no shared or generic IDs, and need-to-know / least-privilege principles.
There is a formal password policy: no sharing, forced change at first login, periodic changes, complexity, and secure storage.
Good password practice is enforced in the solution itself (a minimum length, mixed case, digits and special characters).
Accounts are locked or disabled after a defined number of failed login attempts (a common baseline is 5).
Passwords expire after a defined period (a common baseline is 90-120 days).
Single sign-on (SSO) is supported, so access can be centrally managed and revoked.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Access review & session controls
controls: Access rights to systems, applications and network devices are reviewed at least annually.
Firewall rules are reviewed at least annually.
Workstations lock automatically after a period of inactivity.
Privileged users and administrative tools are subject to specific controls.
Any emergency 'break-glass' accounts that exist are tightly controlled and accounted for.
There is a documented standard for security-event logging: generation, storage, protection, retention, and the attributes captured (date, time, user ID, filename, IP address).
Security-event logs are retained for a defined minimum period (a common baseline is 90 days).

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Change, configuration & patch management
controls: There is a formal change-management process that tracks relevant changes.
Devices are built to a standard configuration and periodically reviewed for deviation.
Servers and endpoints run security software that users cannot disable.
An endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution investigates suspicious activity on hosts and endpoints.
Servers, workstations, applications and network devices are patched on a regular basis.
There is an emergency-patch process for rapid response to critical vulnerabilities.
There is a formal vulnerability-assessment policy: regular assessments, severity classification, and required remediation of high-risk findings.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Backup & monitoring
controls: Systems holding sensitive data are backed up on a regular basis.
Restoration of backups is tested regularly.
External network connections are monitored by an IPS/IDS.
Physical equipment is subject to a regular maintenance process.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Networks & communications
controls: Email systems are protected by technical security controls.
Insecure protocols (Telnet, FTP, unencrypted instant messaging) are disabled at the network boundary.
Sensitive data is encrypted, in transit and on physical media, before it leaves the environment.
Anti-DDoS mechanisms are in place at infrastructure and application level.
Internet access is monitored, and access to known-harmful sites is blocked.
Phishing defenses (email filtering, simulation or training, or similar) are in place.

extra.label: Are subcontractors or sub-processors used to perform the service?

note.label: Name their role (not their identity, if that's easier) and how their access is controlled

controls: Where the solution is hosted by another third party, that hosting contract incorporates information-security requirements.
There are information-security policies governing supplier relationships and the risk of supplier access to assets.
The security of the organization's own suppliers is actively monitored.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Cryptography & key management
controls: Connections between servers and back-office systems are encrypted (e.g. TLS 1.2 or higher, or IPsec).
Data is encrypted at rest (e.g. AES-256 or equivalent).
Passwords are never stored in plaintext - only salted hashes are used to identify users.
There is a defined policy on the use of cryptographic controls: what must be encrypted, mobile/removable media, the key-management approach, applicable standards, and roles.
There is a defined key-management procedure covering the full key lifecycle: generation, storage, archival, retrieval, distribution, removal and destruction.
Unique encryption keys can be issued on a per-customer basis.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Threat & incident management
controls: Employees are contractually obliged to report security incidents.
There is a formal incident-response process: an obligation to report, client notification in the event of a breach, and a response team with defined roles.
There is an emergency-response process for a fast, effective reaction to serious attacks.
Relevant authorities are notified where criminal or fraudulent activity is suspected.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Physical security & business continuity
controls: Buildings housing critical facilities are protected against unauthorized access.
Critical facilities are protected against fire, flood and other environmental hazards.
Critical-facility equipment is protected from power failure and, where needed, climate-controlled.
The solution, and your data within it, is hosted in a clearly defined, secure location.
Critical facilities are protected by surveillance, alarm and intrusion-detection systems.
A continuity plan is in place, based on a risk assessment, for the event of a disaster.
There is a business-continuity clause or SLA covering the recovery plan, recovery time and recovery point objectives.
Business-continuity tests are performed annually, with results, lessons learned and action plans reported to customers.

TPSA_DOMAINS.title: Compliance, monitoring & improvement
controls: There is an established program covering legal, regulatory and contractual requirements (e.g. GDPR, PCI DSS) and relevant standards (e.g. ISO/IEC 27001).
There are documented procedures for monitoring information-security compliance across the organization.
Breaches of the security policy, or suspected weaknesses, are reported to you as the customer.
There is a process to transfer part of the risk in the event of an incident (e.g. cyber insurance).
Networks are supported by documentation, including network configuration diagrams.

TPSA_AI_DOMAINS.title: AI / ML - attack resistance
controls: For generative AI/ML applications that interact with users: prompt-injection attacks are mitigated (e.g. input validation and sanitisation before prompts reach the model).
Model-inversion attacks are mitigated (e.g. privacy-preserving techniques, restricted model access, monitoring).
Training or model data-poisoning attacks are mitigated (e.g. strict data validation and anomaly detection on training and deployment inputs).
Model-theft is mitigated (e.g. limiting the specificity of model outputs, or encrypting model files).
The trained model is isolated from other customers' data and information.

TPSA_AI_DOMAINS.title: AI / ML - data handling & assurance
controls: Data ingested by the AI model is hosted in a clearly defined, secure location, in line with GDPR (EU hosting where required).
The AI system's data handling, model security and deployment environment are audited regularly (e.g. penetration testing).
The AI solution holds relevant AI-specific certification (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001).
The AI solution has documented test reports evaluating its accuracy and performance.

privacy.label: Privacy Assessment
privacy.intro: Screen a process end to end: what data, whose, for what purposes, on what lawful basis, with what retention, who it is shared with and where it goes. It gives a risk level and says whether a full DPIA is needed. If it is, it hands straight over.

dpia.label: Full DPIA
dpia.intro: The full assessment that follows when the Privacy Assessment says a DPIA is needed: necessity and proportionality, individual rights, transfers, the harms the processing could cause individuals rated before and after mitigation, and the three feared security events, all plotted on one severity × likelihood matrix.

lia.label: Legitimate Interest Test
lia.intro: The three-part test for relying on legitimate interests: is the interest legitimate, is the processing necessary for it, and do the individual’s interests override it? Weighs both sides and shows the reasoning.

ai.label: AI Risk Assessment
ai.intro: An EU AI Act-aligned risk assessment: register the AI system, screen it for prohibited/high-risk status, and check autonomy, data, and governance controls.

incident.label: Incident & Breach Severity
incident.intro: Record a privacy incident and, where it qualifies as a personal data breach, score its severity using the published ENISA method - SE = (DPC × EI) + CB - with an analysis of what drives the score and what would change it.

tpsa.label: Third-Party Security Assessment
tpsa.intro: A detailed vendor security questionnaire across governance, people, assets, development, access, operations, cryptography, incident response, physical security, continuity and compliance - plus an AI/ML supplement - scored as inherent risk tempered by control maturity, with a full list of gaps to close.
